brief.aim: The table was evidently assembled for diagnosing heart-disease presence: heart_disease_binary is a two-level outcome (164 vs 139), and the remaining columns are routine clinical/exercise-test measurements taken at the same examination. 'num' is the original 0-4 angiographic severity score from which the binary flag was collapsed, so it is a raw-score component of the target and must be excluded from features rather than predicted. There is no row key, no repeated-subject column and no chronological ordering, so grouping and time constraints stay empty.
brief.repeated_subjects: None apparent; 303 rows and no subject/record key, so each row is treated as a distinct patient.
brief.unit: Patient record from the Cleveland heart-disease cohort (one row per patient encounter).
